source.text: וַיִּוָּעַ֣ץ דָּוִ֗יד עִם־שָׂרֵ֧י הָאֲלָפִ֛ים וְהַמֵּא֖וֹת לְכָל־נָגִֽיד׃

records.literal_gloss: And consulted David with [the] commanders of the thousands and the hundreds, with every leader.

en.L: And David consulted with the commanders of the thousands and of the hundreds, with every ruler.
en.B: David consulted with the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, with every one of the leaders.
en.R: David asked for the advice of the army commanders, the officers over units of a thousand and of a hundred, and of all the leaders.

decisions.choice: verses 1-5 are found only in Chronicles; verses 6-14 retell 2 Samuel 6:2-11
decisions.reason: Chronicles begins the story of the ark with David taking counsel with the leaders and the whole assembly (verses 1-4), which 2 Samuel does not tell; there David simply gathers chosen men (2 Samuel 6:1). From verse 6 the story follows 2 Samuel 6:2-11 closely. Chronicles also places it differently: here it comes straight after David is made king and takes Jerusalem (chapters 11-12), and David's house, family and wars against the Philistines follow in chapter 14, while 2 Samuel tells those first (2 Samuel 5:11-25).

decisions.choice: consulted: took counsel, talked the plan over
decisions.reason: The verb means to take counsel or ask for advice. David does not act alone: he puts the plan to his officers and then to the whole assembly (verses 2-4).

decisions.choice: commanders of thousands and of hundreds: officers over army units
decisions.reason: These were the officers over the larger and smaller units of the army (1 Samuel 22:7; 2 Samuel 18:1). On the size of a "thousand" see the note at Numbers 1:21.

decisions.choice: with every leader: and with all the leaders
decisions.reason: The small word that joins this phrase may sum up the officers just named ("that is, with every leader") or add a further group ("and with every leader"). The word for "leader" is used of the ruler God appoints over his people (11:2), and here of leaders in general. Either way David consults everyone in authority.

decisions.choice: the army commanders, the officers over units of a thousand and of a hundred
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly who the commanders of thousands and of hundreds were, and "asked for the advice of" for "consulted with".

decisions.choice: ruler (Literal); leaders (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "ruler" for this word throughout these books (11:2). Here it names leaders in general, not a king, so Balanced and Readable say "leaders", as at 12:28.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜יד לְכֹ֣ל׀קְהַ֣ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אִם־עֲלֵיכֶ֨ם ט֜וֹב וּמִן־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ נִפְרְצָה֙ נִשְׁלְחָ֞ה עַל־אַחֵ֣ינוּ הַנִּשְׁאָרִ֗ים בְּכֹל֙ אַרְצ֣וֹת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְעִמָּהֶ֛ם הַכֹּהֲנִ֥ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֖ם בְּעָרֵ֣י מִגְרְשֵׁיהֶ֑ם וְיִקָּבְצ֖וּ אֵלֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said David to all [the] assembly of Israel, If upon you [it is] good, and from Yahweh our God, let us break out, let us send to our brothers the remaining in all [the] lands of Israel, and with them the priests and the Levites in [the] cities of their pasturelands, and let them gather to us.

en.L: And David said to all the assembly of Israel, "If [it is] good to you, and [if it is] from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, let us spread out, let us send to our brothers who remain in all the lands of Israel, and with them the priests and the Levites in the cities of their pasturelands, and let them gather to us.
en.B: Then David said to the whole assembly of Israel, "If you approve, and if this comes from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, let us send out in every direction to our fellow Israelites who remain in all the territories of Israel, and to the priests and the Levites with them in the towns where they have their pasturelands, so that they may gather to us.
en.R: Then David said to the whole assembly of Israel, "If you think this is good, and if it is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God wants, let us send messengers everywhere. Let us send them to all our fellow Israelites who are left in every part of Israel, and to the priests and the Levites who live among them in their own towns and pasturelands. Let us ask them all to come and join us.

decisions.choice: two conditions: the assembly's approval and the LORD's will
decisions.reason: David makes the plan depend on two things: that the assembly agrees, and that it comes from the LORD. The second clause has no verb; "from the LORD our God" means that the plan has his approval. The assembly gives its answer in verse 4.

decisions.choice: let us break out, let us send: let us send out far and wide
decisions.reason: The first verb means "break out, spread out" and is not joined to another verb this way anywhere else. Together the two seem to mean sending out in every direction, without holding back. Others take it as "let us send quickly", or read the first word slightly differently. The same verb "break out" returns when the LORD breaks out against Uzzah (verse 11; 15:13).

decisions.choice: our brothers who remain in all the lands of Israel: the rest of the people in every tribe's territory
decisions.reason: "Brothers" here means fellow members of the people of Israel (Deuteronomy 17:15). "Who remain" most likely means those still at home in their own territories, not present at the meeting; it may also recall that the people had been left few and scattered after Saul's defeat (10:7). "The lands of Israel" are the territories of the tribes.

decisions.choice: the priests and the Levites in the towns with pasturelands
decisions.reason: The Levites had no tribal territory of their own but were given towns with grazing land around them among the other tribes (Numbers 35:1-8; Joshua 21; 1 Chronicles 6:39-66). David calls them too because the ark was in their charge (15:2).

decisions.choice: our fellow Israelites
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "fellow Israelites" for "brothers", the members of the nation, so that the word is not taken to mean brothers by birth.

decisions.choice: let us send messengers everywhere ... Let us ask them all to come and join us
decisions.reason: Readable splits the long sentence into three, says who is sent, and turns "and let them gather to us" into a request to come.

source.text: וְנָסֵ֛בָּה אֶת־אֲר֥וֹן אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ אֵלֵ֑ינוּ כִּי־לֹ֥א דְרַשְׁנֻ֖הוּ בִּימֵ֥י שָׁאֽוּל׃

records.literal_gloss: And let us bring around [the] ark of our God to us, for not we sought it in [the] days of Saul.

en.L: And let us bring back the ark of our God to us, for we did not seek it in the days of Saul."
en.B: Then let us bring the ark of our God back to us, for we did not seek it in the days of Saul."
en.R: Then let us bring the ark of our God back here to us. While Saul was king, we did not seek it."

decisions.choice: bring back: bring around to where we are
decisions.reason: The verb means "turn around" or "bring round". The ark had stayed in Kiriath-jearim, away from the people's life and worship, since the Philistines sent it back (1 Samuel 6:21-7:2). David proposes to bring it back among the people.

decisions.choice: seek it: the ark
decisions.reason: The ending on the verb can mean "it" or "him". The nearest noun is "the ark of our God", so it is read as "it": to come to the ark to worship and to ask God's guidance there, which Saul did only once (1 Samuel 14:18). Read as "him", the words would echo 10:13-14, where Saul died because he did not seek the LORD. The sense is close either way, since to seek the ark was to seek the God whose presence it marked.

decisions.choice: we did not seek: a key word in Chronicles
decisions.reason: To "seek" God means to turn to him in worship and trust, and Chronicles uses the word often (10:13-14; 16:10-11; 22:19; 28:9). David says "we": the neglect was the people's, not Saul's alone. When the ark is finally brought up, David says the first attempt failed because "we did not seek him in the proper way" (15:13).

decisions.choice: While Saul was king
decisions.reason: Readable says "while Saul was king" for "in the days of Saul" and puts it first.

source.text: וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ כָֽל־הַקָּהָ֖ל לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת כֵּ֑ן כִּֽי־יָשַׁ֥ר הַדָּבָ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֥י כָל־הָעָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said all the assembly to do so, for was right the thing in [the] eyes of all the people.

en.L: And all the assembly said to do so, for the thing was right in the eyes of all the people.
en.B: The whole assembly agreed to do this, because the plan seemed right to all the people.
en.R: The whole assembly agreed to do it, because all the people thought it was the right thing to do.

decisions.choice: said to do so: agreed to act on it
decisions.reason: "Said to do so" means that the assembly answered yes to David's proposal and resolved to carry it out.

decisions.choice: right in the eyes of all the people: it seemed right to them
decisions.reason: "Right in someone's eyes" means that a plan pleased them or seemed good to them (1 Samuel 18:20, 26; 2 Samuel 17:4). Chronicles stresses that the whole people agreed.

decisions.choice: agreed
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "agreed" for "said to do so", and "the plan" or "it" for "the thing".

source.text: וַיַּקְהֵ֤ל דָּוִיד֙ אֶת־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִן־שִׁיח֥וֹר מִצְרַ֖יִם וְעַד־לְב֣וֹא חֲמָ֑ת לְהָבִיא֙ אֶת־אֲר֣וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים מִקִּרְיַ֖ת יְעָרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And assembled David all Israel from Shihor of Egypt and to Lebo Hamath, to bring [the] ark of the God from Kiriath-jearim.

en.L: And David assembled all Israel, from Shihor of Egypt and to Lebo-hamath, to bring the ark of God from Kiriath-jearim.
en.B: So David assembled all Israel, from the Shihor of Egypt as far as Lebo-hamath, to bring the ark of God from Kiriath-jearim.
en.R: So David called together all the people of Israel, from the Shihor on the border of Egypt in the south to Lebo-hamath in the far north. They came to bring the ark of God from Kiriath-jearim.

decisions.choice: Shihor of Egypt: the southern edge of the land
decisions.reason: The name Shihor is used of a stream at Egypt's edge (Joshua 13:3) and of the Nile (Isaiah 23:3). Here it marks the southern limit of the land, on the border of Egypt, near what Numbers 34:5 calls the Brook of Egypt. Its exact place is not known.

decisions.choice: Lebo-hamath: the northern edge of the land
decisions.reason: Lebo-hamath, "the entrance of Hamath" or the town of Lebo on the way to Hamath, is the northern limit of the promised land (Numbers 34:8; Joshua 13:5).

decisions.choice: from Shihor to Lebo-hamath: all Israel, from one end of the land to the other
decisions.reason: The same two limits mark the whole land in Joshua 13:3-5, and Solomon's people come "from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of Egypt" when the temple is dedicated (1 Kings 8:65). The whole people, from south to north, takes part in bringing the ark.

decisions.choice: Kiriath-jearim: where the ark had stayed
decisions.reason: After the Philistines sent the ark back, it was taken to the house of Abinadab in Kiriath-jearim and stayed there for many years (1 Samuel 7:1-2).

decisions.choice: on the border of Egypt in the south; in the far north; They came
decisions.reason: Readable says where the two places lay, so that the reader sees that the whole land is meant, and begins a new sentence for the purpose.

source.text: וַיַּ֨עַל דָּוִ֤יד וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בַּעֲלָ֔תָה אֶל־קִרְיַ֥ת יְעָרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר לִיהוּדָ֑ה לְהַעֲל֣וֹת מִשָּׁ֗ם אֵת֩ אֲר֨וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֧ים׀יְהוָ֛ה יוֹשֵׁ֥ב הַכְּרוּבִ֖ים אֲשֶׁר־נִקְרָ֥א שֵֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And went up David and all Israel to Baalah, to Kiriath-jearim which [belongs] to Judah, to bring up from there [the] ark of the God, Yahweh, sitting [on] the cherubim, which is called [the] name.

en.L: And David and all Israel went up to Baalah, to Kiriath-jearim, which [belongs] to Judah, to bring up from there the ark of God, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who sits [on] the cherubim, which is called [by the] name.
en.B: David and all Israel went up to Baalah, that is, Kiriath-jearim, which belongs to Judah, to bring the ark of God up from there, the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who sits enthroned on the cherubim, the ark which is called by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.
en.R: Then David and all Israel went up to Baalah, which is Kiriath-jearim in Judah. They went to bring the ark of God up from there. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} sits as king above the cherubim, the winged creatures on the lid of the ark, and the ark bears {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.

decisions.choice: Baalah, that is Kiriath-jearim, which belongs to Judah
decisions.reason: Baalah is an older name for Kiriath-jearim (Joshua 15:9; also called Kiriath-baal, Joshua 15:60). The town lay on Judah's northern border (Joshua 18:14). Chronicles gives both names so that the reader knows the place.

decisions.choice: the differences from 2 Samuel 6:2
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 6:2 says that David and "all the people who were with him" set out "from Baale-judah"; Chronicles says that David and "all Israel" went up "to Baalah, to Kiriath-jearim, which belongs to Judah", explaining the old name and making the town the goal of the journey (see the note at 2 Samuel 6:2 on "from" and "to"). The ark's title is also shorter: 2 Samuel has "the ark of God, which is called by the name, the name of the LORD of hosts, who sits on the cherubim over it"; Chronicles has "the ark of God, the LORD who sits on the cherubim, which is called by the name", without "of hosts" and "over it", with "name" once, and with the LORD's name straight after "God".

decisions.choice: which is called by the name: the ark, called by the LORD's name
alternatives: where his name is called on
decisions.reason: The last clause has no stated subject. It most likely refers to the ark, which is "called by the name" of the LORD, that is, belongs to him, as 2 Samuel 6:2 says more fully (Deuteronomy 28:10; Jeremiah 7:10-11). It can also be read of the LORD, "whose name is called on there". Either way the LORD's name is linked to the ark.

decisions.choice: sits: sits enthroned, reigns
decisions.reason: As in 1 Samuel 4:4 and 2 Samuel 6:2, the verb "sit" said of a king means to sit on a throne. The LORD is pictured as king seated above the cherubim on the ark's cover, with the ark as his footstool (28:2; Psalm 99:1).

decisions.choice: that is; by his name
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "that is" to show that Baalah and Kiriath-jearim are one town, and "his" to say whose name is meant (m3).

decisions.choice: sits as king above the cherubim, the winged creatures on the lid of the ark, and the ark bears his name
decisions.reason: Readable explains the cherubim in the words used at 2 Samuel 6:2 and says in a new sentence that the ark bears the LORD's name.

source.text: וַיַּרְכִּ֜יבוּ אֶת־אֲר֤וֹן הָאֱלֹהִים֙ עַל־עֲגָלָ֣ה חֲדָשָׁ֔ה מִבֵּ֖ית אֲבִינָדָ֑ב וְעֻזָּ֣א וְאַחְי֔וֹ נֹהֲגִ֖ים בָּעֲגָלָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they made ride [the] ark of the God on [a] cart new from [the] house of Abinadab; and Uzzah and Ahio [were] driving the cart.

en.L: And they carried the ark of God on a new cart from the house of Abinadab; and Uzzah and Ahio [were] driving the cart.
en.B: They carried the ark of God on a new cart from Abinadab's house, while Uzzah and Ahio drove the cart.
en.R: They put the ark of God on a new cart and took it from Abinadab's house. Uzzah and Ahio were guiding the cart.

decisions.choice: on a new cart: carried by oxen instead of on men's shoulders
decisions.reason: A new cart, never used for ordinary work, was a mark of respect. But it was how the Philistines had sent the ark back (1 Samuel 6:7-8). The law gave the holy things to the Levites of Kohath to carry on their shoulders with poles (Exodus 25:14; Numbers 4:15; 7:9). When David tried again, the Levites carried the ark in that way (15:2, 15), and David said the first attempt failed because they had not sought the LORD in the proper way (15:13).

decisions.choice: the differences from 2 Samuel 6:3-4
decisions.reason: Chronicles tells this more briefly than 2 Samuel 6:3-4. It does not say that Abinadab's house was "on the hill" or that Uzzah and Ahio were "the sons of Abinadab", and it has neither the words that 2 Samuel 6:4 repeats from 6:3 nor "Ahio was walking before the ark". It says "driving the cart", where 2 Samuel says "the new cart". Chronicles writes Uzzah's name with a different last letter throughout; he is the same man.

decisions.choice: carried
decisions.reason: The verb means "made to ride". At 2 Samuel 6:3 Literal says "set ... on", because a second verb, "and carried it", follows there; here the one verb covers the whole journey from Abinadab's house, so Literal and Balanced say "carried". Readable keeps the wording of 2 Samuel 6:3.

decisions.choice: guiding the cart
decisions.reason: As at 2 Samuel 6:3: the men walked beside the oxen and steered them.

source.text: וְדָוִ֣יד וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל מְשַׂחֲקִ֛ים לִפְנֵ֥י הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּכָל־עֹ֑ז וּבְשִׁירִ֤ים וּבְכִנֹּרוֹת֙ וּבִנְבָלִ֣ים וּבְתֻפִּ֔ים וּבִמְצִלְתַּ֖יִם וּבַחֲצֹצְרֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And David and all Israel [were] celebrating before the God with all strength, and with songs and with lyres and with harps and with tambourines and with cymbals and with trumpets.

en.L: And David and all Israel [were] celebrating before God with all strength, and with songs and with lyres and with harps and with tambourines and with cymbals and with trumpets.
en.B: David and all Israel were celebrating before God with all their might, with songs and with lyres, harps, tambourines, cymbals and trumpets.
en.R: David and all Israel were celebrating in front of God with all their strength. They sang songs and played lyres, harps, tambourines, cymbals and trumpets.

decisions.choice: celebrating: making merry with music and dance
decisions.reason: The verb means "laugh, play, make merry", as at 2 Samuel 6:5. It is used of dancing in celebration (1 Samuel 18:7; Jeremiah 31:4), and Michal sees David "dancing and celebrating" when the ark comes into the city (15:29).

decisions.choice: the differences from 2 Samuel 6:5
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 6:5 has "all the house of Israel" celebrating "before the LORD with all kinds of cypress wood"; Chronicles has "all Israel" celebrating "before God with all strength and with songs". In Hebrew the two readings share many letters, and one may have come from the other in copying (see the note at 2 Samuel 6:5). The list of instruments also differs: Chronicles has no rattles and adds trumpets.

decisions.choice: before God: in front of the ark, where God was present
decisions.reason: The ark marked the place of God's presence (verse 6), so to celebrate before the ark was to celebrate before God himself.

decisions.choice: lyres, harps, tambourines, cymbals and trumpets
decisions.reason: The lyre and the harp were stringed instruments, the lyre the smaller; the tambourine was a hand drum; cymbals were struck metal plates (see 2 Samuel 6:5). The trumpets were the metal trumpets blown by the priests (Numbers 10:2, 8; 1 Chronicles 15:24; 16:6).

decisions.choice: with all their might
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "their": it is the people's own strength that is meant. Readable adds "sang" and "played" to say what was done with the songs and instruments.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ עַד־גֹּ֣רֶן כִּידֹ֑ן וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח עֻזָּ֜א אֶת־יָד֗וֹ לֶאֱחֹז֙ אֶת־הָ֣אָר֔וֹן כִּ֥י שָֽׁמְט֖וּ הַבָּקָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And they came to [the] threshing floor of Chidon, and put out Uzzah his hand to take hold of the ark, for stumbled the oxen.

en.L: And they came to the threshing floor of Chidon, and Uzzah put out his hand to take hold of the ark, for the oxen stumbled.
en.B: When they arrived at the threshing floor of Chidon, Uzzah put out his hand to take hold of the ark, for the oxen had stumbled.
en.R: When they reached the threshing floor of Chidon, the oxen stumbled. Uzzah reached out his hand to grab the ark and steady it.

decisions.choice: the threshing floor of Chidon; put out his hand to take hold of the ark
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 6:6 calls the place "the threshing floor of Nacon". Whether these are two names for one place, or one name changed in copying, is not known. 2 Samuel also says only that Uzzah "sent to the ark of God and took hold of it"; Chronicles says "put out his hand to take hold of the ark". A threshing floor was a flat open space where grain was threshed.

decisions.choice: the oxen stumbled: the cart lurched
decisions.reason: As at 2 Samuel 6:6: the verb means "let drop" or "let loose", and probably says that the oxen stumbled or slipped, so that the ark was in danger of falling.

decisions.choice: the oxen stumbled; to grab the ark and steady it
decisions.reason: As at 2 Samuel 6:6, Readable tells the events in the order they happened and says why Uzzah took hold.

source.text: וַיִּֽחַר־אַ֤ף יְהוָה֙ בְּעֻזָּ֔א וַיַּכֵּ֕הוּ עַ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־שָׁלַ֥ח יָד֖וֹ עַל־הָאָר֑וֹן וַיָּ֥מָת שָׁ֖ם לִפְנֵ֥י אֱלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And burned [the] anger of Yahweh against Uzzah, and he struck him because that he put out his hand on the ark; and he died there before God.

en.L: And the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} burned against Uzzah, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} struck him because he put out his hand on the ark; and he died there before God.
en.B: Then the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} blazed against Uzzah, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} struck him down because he had put out his hand to the ark. He died there before God.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was very angry with Uzzah. He struck him down because Uzzah had put his hand on the ark, and Uzzah died there in front of God.

decisions.choice: the differences from 2 Samuel 6:7
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 6:7 says that "God struck him there for the error, and he died there beside the ark of God". Chronicles says that the LORD struck him "because he put out his hand to the ark", and that he died "before God". The rare word in 2 Samuel probably names the same fault, and Chronicles states it plainly (see the note at 2 Samuel 6:7).

decisions.choice: the LORD's anger against Uzzah: the holiness of the ark
decisions.reason: The law warned that even the Levites who carried the holy things must not touch them, or they would die (Numbers 4:15), and many at Beth-shemesh had died for looking into the ark (1 Samuel 6:19). Uzzah meant to protect the ark, but it was holy, and it was being moved in a way the law did not allow (verse 7; 15:13). The text tells what happened and does not explain further.

decisions.choice: before God: in God's presence, beside the ark
decisions.reason: Uzzah died where he stood, beside the ark, which marked God's presence (verses 6, 8).

decisions.choice: was very angry
decisions.reason: As at 2 Samuel 6:7: Readable says "was very angry" for the picture of anger that "burned", and names Uzzah where "he" could be unclear.

source.text: וַיִּ֣חַר לְדָוִ֔יד כִּֽי־פָרַ֧ץ יְהוָ֛ה פֶּ֖רֶץ בְּעֻזָּ֑א וַיִּקְרָ֞א לַמָּק֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ פֶּ֣רֶץ עֻזָּ֔א עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it burned to David because broke out Yahweh [a] breaking out against Uzzah; and he called the place that Perez-uzzah until the day the this.

en.L: And David was angry because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had broken out [with] a breaking out against Uzzah; and he called that place Perez-uzzah, to this day.
en.B: David was angry because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had burst out against Uzzah, and he named that place Perez-uzzah, a name it still has to this day.
en.R: David was angry because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had burst out against Uzzah. So he named that place Perez-uzzah, which means "bursting out against Uzzah". It still has that name to this day.

decisions.choice: David was angry
decisions.reason: As at 2 Samuel 6:8: the verb is the same "burn" used of the LORD's anger in verse 10, here without the word "anger". It may also mean that David was deeply upset (Jonah 4:1, 4). The text does not say whether his anger was against the LORD, against himself, or at what had happened.

decisions.choice: broke out ... Perez-uzzah: the same words as 2 Samuel 6:8
decisions.reason: This verse is the same as 2 Samuel 6:8 except for the spelling of Uzzah's name. The verb "break out" and the noun from it give the place its name, "breaking out against Uzzah". The people had planned to "spread out" with the same verb (verse 2); now the LORD breaks out against them. In Chronicles David names Baal-perazim, where the LORD broke out against his enemies, only after this (14:11), and he looks back on this day in 15:13: "the LORD our God broke out against us".

decisions.choice: to this day: the day the account was written
decisions.reason: As at 2 Samuel 6:8 and 4:41: the name was still in use when the account was written.

decisions.choice: which means "bursting out against Uzzah"
decisions.reason: As at 2 Samuel 6:8, Readable explains the meaning of the name, which a Hebrew reader would hear at once.

source.text: וַיִּירָ֤א דָוִיד֙ אֶת־הָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא לֵאמֹ֑ר הֵ֚יךְ אָבִ֣יא אֵלַ֔י אֵ֖ת אֲר֥וֹן הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And feared David the God on the day the that, saying, How will I bring to me the ark of the God?

en.L: And David feared God on that day, saying, "How shall I bring the ark of God to me?"
en.B: David was afraid of God that day, and he said, "How can I ever bring the ark of God to me?"
en.R: That day David was afraid of God. He said, "How can I ever bring the ark of God here to stay with me?"

decisions.choice: feared God: was afraid of him
decisions.reason: As at 2 Samuel 6:9: the verb can mean reverence or awe, but here, after Uzzah's death, it is plain fear of what God might do.

decisions.choice: the differences from 2 Samuel 6:9
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 6:9 says that David "feared the LORD" and asked, "How shall the ark of the LORD come to me?" Chronicles says "feared God" and "the ark of God", and makes David the one who acts: "How shall I bring the ark of God to me?" The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: How shall I bring ...?: a question of fear and doubt
decisions.reason: The question does not ask for a method. It means that David no longer dares to bring the ark into his own city (verse 13).

decisions.choice: here to stay with me
decisions.reason: As at 2 Samuel 6:9, Readable adds that the ark was to stay with David in his city.

source.text: וְלֹֽא־הֵסִ֨יר דָּוִ֧יד אֶת־הָאָר֛וֹן אֵלָ֖יו אֶל־עִ֣יר דָּוִ֑יד וַיַּטֵּ֕הוּ אֶל־בֵּ֥ית עֹבֵֽד־אֱדֹ֖ם הַגִּתִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And not turned aside David the ark to himself to [the] city of David, and he turned it aside to [the] house of Obed-Edom the Gittite.

en.L: And David did not move the ark to himself, into the city of David; and he turned it aside to the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite.
en.B: So David did not take the ark into the city of David to be with him. Instead he turned aside and took it to the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite.
en.R: So David did not take the ark home with him to the city of David. Instead, he had it taken off the road to the house of a man named Obed-Edom, who came from Gath.

decisions.choice: the differences from 2 Samuel 6:10
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 6:10 says that David "was not willing" to move "the ark of the LORD" to himself, and that "David" turned it aside. Chronicles says simply that he did not move "the ark", and has "he" in the second clause. The story is the same.

decisions.choice: the city of David: the stronghold of Zion
decisions.reason: David had captured the stronghold of Zion and it was called the city of David (11:5, 7). It was the oldest part of Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: Obed-Edom the Gittite: a man from a town called Gath
decisions.reason: "Gittite" means a man from Gath. This could be the Philistine city, since David had men from there among his followers (2 Samuel 15:18-19). It could also be Gath-rimmon, a town given to the Levites (Joshua 21:24-25), and Chronicles names an Obed-Edom among the Levite gatekeepers and musicians who served the ark (15:18, 24; 16:38; 26:4). The text here does not say which.

decisions.choice: had it taken off the road; who came from Gath
decisions.reason: As at 2 Samuel 6:10, Readable says plainly what "turned it aside" and "Gittite" mean.

source.text: וַיֵּשֶׁב֩ אֲר֨וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֜ים עִם־בֵּ֨ית עֹבֵ֥ד אֱדֹ֛ם בְּבֵית֖וֹ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה חֳדָשִׁ֑ים וַיְבָ֧רֶךְ יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־בֵּ֥ית עֹבֵֽד־אֱדֹ֖ם וְאֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־לֽוֹ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And remained [the] ark of the God with [the] household of Obed-Edom in his house three months; and blessed Yahweh [the] household of Obed-Edom and all that [was] to him.

en.L: And the ark of God remained with the household of Obed-Edom in his house three months, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} blessed the household of Obed-Edom and all that [was] his.
en.B: The ark of God stayed for three months with the household of Obed-Edom in his house, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} blessed Obed-Edom's household and everything he had.
en.R: The ark of God stayed with Obed-Edom's family in his house for three months. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} blessed Obed-Edom's family and everything he owned.

decisions.choice: the differences from 2 Samuel 6:11
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 6:11 says that "the ark of the LORD remained at the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite" and that the LORD "blessed Obed-Edom and all his household". Chronicles says that "the ark of God remained with the household of Obed-Edom in his house", making clear that the ark stayed inside his home with his family, and that the LORD "blessed the household of Obed-Edom and all that he had", words close to those reported to David in 2 Samuel 6:12. In Chronicles the three months frame chapter 14, before the ark is brought up in chapter 15.

decisions.choice: household ... house: the family, then the building
decisions.reason: The same word is used twice with two senses: first the household, his family and those who lived under his care, and then his house, the building where the ark stayed.

decisions.choice: the LORD blessed Obed-Edom's household: the ark brings blessing as well as judgment
decisions.reason: The same ark that brought death to Uzzah brought good to the household that kept it. Chronicles later lists the many sons God gave Obed-Edom, "for God had blessed him" (26:4-5).

decisions.choice: family; everything he owned
decisions.reason: Readable says "family" for "household" and "everything he owned" for "all that was his".
